title: Codebook wording review: Facts about each source page
background:
Review round 4 of the codebook wording. You chose on 30 October that agents draft the missing value definitions and you review every wording slot here. This page covers **facts about each source page**.

Each card is one codebook item. Open "Show the wording slots" to read them. Each slot is labelled with where its text came from:

- **Plan text**
- **New agent draft (round 4)**
- **Option text you chose in round 3**
- **Agent edit of the signed questionnaire**
- **Text you approved on 30 October**
- **Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete**

Answer per item: approve all, approve with line-edits or deletions in the comments (by slot number), or ask for a redraft. Deletion is open only for old version-2.5 slots and for one slot of each overlap pair. The batch card at the top approves everything you leave unmarked. No recommendation is given on any wording.

New agent drafts carry a certainty mark; those marked **Needs your decision** rest on no ruling or text for some point.

items.title: source type
items.situation:
Recorded per source page.

10 slots: 8 × old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete; 2 × plan text.
items.body:
**1. Value `news_major`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Major national/international news outlet (Reuters, BBC, NYT, Le Monde, NHK, etc.)

**2. Value `news_trade`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Technology or government trade press (GovTech, FedScoop, PublicTechnology, etc.)

**3. Value `vendor`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Vendor website, case study, blog post, or press release

**4. Value `academic`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Peer-reviewed paper, working paper, university report

**5. Value `policy_org`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Think tank, IGO, or policy organization (OECD, World Bank, ITU, Brookings, etc.)

**6. Value `social_media`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Official social media accounts (Twitter/X, LinkedIn from institutional accounts)

**7. Value `procurement_tender`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
Tender notice, RFP, contract award, vendor selection document

**8. Value `other`** — Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete · may be deleted
None of the above; explain in `source_snippet`

**9. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 2
'Official' comes from the domain field and 'archive' from the address; the classifier only sorts the rest (news, vendor, academic, policy organisation, social media, procurement, other). The question wording is amended.

**10. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 2
Source type is answered by the same classifier question in every pipeline where it applies. The AI-text pipeline drops its genre table and procurement's fixed value is replaced.
